identification.summary: ESET describes GopherWhisper as a previously undocumented China-aligned APT group that targets governmental institutions in Mongolia [S1][S2]. ESET found it in January 2025 after discovering a new backdoor, LaxGopher, on the system of a Mongolian government institution [S2][S5]. Most of its tools are written in Go, with a C++ fallback backdoor, SSLORDoor [S1]. It uses Discord, Slack, Microsoft 365 Outlook and file.io for command and control (C2) and exfiltration [S2][S3].
identification.firstObserved: ESET assesses the group has been active since at least November 2023 (as reported by secondary coverage); ESET first discovered it in January 2025 [S3][S5].
identification.notes: No Microsoft actor name or MITRE ATT&CK group ID was found for GopherWhisper in the sources gathered. The name is ESET's. ESET reportedly found no links between the toolset and known groups, which led to a new cluster designation [S5]. Do not merge with other China-aligned clusters without vendor evidence.

attribution.confidence: ESET characterizes the group as China-aligned and says the activity looks like cyber espionage, but reportedly did not tie it to a specific entity [S1][S3]. No government attribution was found.
attribution.basis: Per coverage of ESET's report: Slack and Discord message timestamps cluster in 08:00-17:00 UTC+8 (China Standard Time), and a Slack locale setting and VMware machine timestamps point the same way [S3]. The toolset reportedly showed no links to known groups [S5].

objectives: ESET characterizes the activity as cyber espionage against a Mongolian government institution [S1][S3]. Specific collection requirements are not stated in the sources gathered. CompactGopher compresses files and uploads them to file.io, which indicates document collection [S3].

regions: Possible additional victims in unidentified locations and sectors [S2]
targeting.notes: The confirmed victim is a Mongolian governmental institution, with about 12 infected systems reported there [S4][S7]. ESET's analysis of C2 traffic via attacker-controlled Discord and Slack suggests dozens of other entities were compromised; their locations and sectors are unknown [S2][S3]. The imported record says Central Asia; that regional claim was not found in the sources gathered.

capabilities.summary: ESET documents a toolset of custom Go backdoors LaxGopher (Slack C2), RatGopher (Discord C2) and BoxOfFriends (Microsoft 365 Outlook draft messages via the Microsoft Graph mail REST API), the injector JabGopher, the exfiltration tool CompactGopher (compresses files and uploads to file.io), the loader FriendDelivery, and the C++ backdoor SSLORDoor [S2][S3][S4]. The group abuses legitimate cloud services for C2 and exfiltration, tested malware on these platforms, then reused the same accounts for live operations without clearing logs [S3][S4]. The initial access vector was not found in the sources gathered.

diamond.adversary: China-aligned espionage group tracked by ESET as GopherWhisper; working hours consistent with UTC+8 [S1][S3].
diamond.capability: Go-based backdoors, injector, loader and exfiltration tool, plus a C++ fallback backdoor, using legitimate cloud services for C2 [S2][S3].
diamond.infrastructure: Attacker-controlled Slack and Discord workspaces and channels, Microsoft 365 Outlook accounts (draft messages), file.io for exfiltration [S2][S3]. Per ESET, Slack and Discord API tokens were obtained, allowing retrieval of C2 messages [S2].
diamond.victim: A Mongolian governmental institution (about 12 systems), with dozens of other unidentified victims suspected [S2][S4].
diamond.socioPolitical: Espionage against a Mongolian government body by a China-aligned actor [S1][S3]. Policy drivers were not stated in the sources gathered.
diamond.technology: Windows endpoints and enterprise use of Slack, Discord and Microsoft 365 Outlook, whose traffic is generally allowed and blends with legitimate use [S2][S3].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain is government endpoints and the enterprise SaaS channels (Slack, Discord, Microsoft 365 Outlook) that the actor uses for C2; these are typically allowed through boundary controls [S2][S3]. STEP 2: The actor's use of allowed cloud services reduces the value of domain and IP blocklists [S3]. STEP 3: Observed pattern is backdoor deployment (Go tools), C2 via chat or mail-draft channels, then file compression and upload to file.io [S2][S3]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued espionage against Mongolian and possibly other regional government entities. MDCOA is reuse of the same tradecraft against partner-nation government networks relevant to coalition operations; this is an inference, not a sourced finding. Candidate indicators: unapproved Slack or Discord clients or API token use on government hosts, Graph API mail-draft creation by non-mail processes, and uploads to file.io [S3].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track ESET's IOCs and fold SaaS-abuse detections (chat API tokens, draft-message Graph calls, file.io egress) into hunt plans [S2][S3]. (2) Authorities: monitoring or blocking of commercial chat services on government networks needs owner and policy approval; coordinate before action. (3) Mission assurance: assume cloud-service C2 may bypass perimeter allowlists; verify which SaaS tenants and clients are authorized. (4) Coordination: the confirmed victim is a foreign government, so sharing runs through partner and vendor channels; the platform providers (Slack, Discord, Microsoft) can disable abused accounts.

provenance.importedSummary: GopherWhisper is a China-aligned APT that routes C2 traffic through legitimate enterprise platforms like Slack, Discord, and Microsoft 365 Outlook to evade detection. Its toolkit includes the LaxGopher backdoor for Slack, RatGopher for Discord, and CompactGopher for data exfiltration via file.io. The group employs DLL side-loading via JabGopher and uses raw OpenSSL socket C2 on port 443 with the SSLORDoor backdoor. GopherWhisper has targeted Mongolian government entities and is assessed to have additional unidentified victims in Central Asia.
